Di fronte a una massa renale la prima do:
Faced with a renal mass, the first question is: solid or cystic? A lesion that enhances by more than 20 HU compared with the unenhanced scan is solid. If it contains no macroscopic fat (which points toward angiomyolipoma), a solid renal mass in an adult should be considered a carcinoma until proven otherwise.
Clear cell carcinoma is the most common subtype: it is typically hypervascular, heterogeneous due to necrosis and hemorrhage, with intense enhancement in the corticomedullary phase and washout in the delayed phases. Papillary carcinoma is usually hypovascular and homogeneous; chromophobe carcinoma shows intermediate enhancement.
The report must always describe: size, relationship with the renal sinus and the collecting system, the renal vein and inferior vena cava (tumor thrombus), lymph nodes, the adrenal gland and the contralateral kidney. T stage (TNM 8th ed.; here T1b or T2a depending on whether the maximum diameter is below or above 7 cm: measure it): T1a ≤ 4 cm, T1b 4-7 cm, T2 > 7 cm confined to the kidney, T3a if it invades perirenal or sinus fat or the renal vein, T3b-c if the thrombus reaches the vena cava. The RENAL score can be used to plan partial nephrectomy.
Massa renale solida senza grasso macrosc: Solid renal mass without macroscopic fat: carcinoma until proven otherwise; always look for thrombosis of the renal vein and vena cava.
